channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: US and Venezuela Sign Military Cooperation Deal as Hegseth Makes Surprise Caracas Visit
item.description: The United States and Venezuela have signed a military cooperation agreement covering joint training and intelligence sharing, announced by US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth during a surprise visit to Caracas on Wednesday.

item.title: UK Government Asks Google to Remove Russell Brand's YouTube Account After Prison Message
item.description: The British government has asked Google to remove Russell Brand's YouTube account after the jailed comedian used the channel to publish a message from prison in which he maintained his innocence.

item.title: Putin's Nuclear Briefcase Spotted at China Summit Ahead of Rare Three-Way Talks
item.description: A naval officer accompanying President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen confirmed on camera that the black briefcase he was carrying is Russia's nuclear command case, a day before Putin is due to meet the American and Chinese leaders together.

item.title: Voyager 1 Becomes First Human-Made Object a Full Light-Day From Earth
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1 has become the first human-made object to travel a full light-day from Earth, reaching about 16 billion miles from home nearly 50 years after launch.

item.title: Russian Strikes on Odesa's Historic Centre Kill Four, Wound Thirteen
item.description: Russian forces struck the historic centre of Odesa three times on Wednesday morning, killing four people and wounding thirteen, Ukrainian officials said.

item.title: Elderly French Parents Jailed 39 Years After Four-Year-Old Daughter's Death
item.description: A French court has jailed an elderly couple over the killing of their four-year-old daughter after prolonged abuse, closing one of France's oldest unsolved cases 39 years after the child's body was found beside a motorway.

item.title: Spanish Court Opens Criminal Investigation Into Julio Iglesias Over Sex Offence Allegations
item.description: Singer Julio Iglesias faces a criminal investigation in Spain after two former employees accused him of sexual offences, assault and degrading treatment.

item.title: Anthropic's Seven Founders Set to Become Multi-Billionaires as AI Giant Goes Public
item.description: The seven people who founded Anthropic are hours away from becoming multi-billionaires, as the company behind the Claude chatbot lists its shares in one of the largest stock market debuts in history.

item.title: US Egg Giant to Cull 1.8 Million Birds After Bird Flu Hits Florida Farm
item.description: The largest egg producer in the United States will cull about 1.8 million birds after bird flu was found at one of its farms in Florida, shutting production at the site for now.

item.title: Democrats Choose Jeffries as Speaker Nominee, Clearing Path to Historic First
item.description: House Democrats have chosen Hakeem Jeffries as their nominee for speaker, putting the New York congressman on course to become the first Black person to hold the post when the new Congress meets in January.

item.title: Iran Says It Brought Down a US Reaper Drone Near the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's army says it brought down an American MQ-9 Reaper drone near the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, in the latest escalation of the nine-month conflict between the United States and Iran.

item.title: William and Kate Meet Modi in New Delhi as Three-Day India Visit Ends
item.description: The Prince and Princess of Wales have met Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, closing a three-day visit to India built around the Earthshot Prize environmental awards.

item.title: Israel Vows to Hold Gaza, Lebanon and Syria Zones Indefinitely as Tanks Push Into Central Gaza
item.description: Israel has launched its first large-scale ground operation in central Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire, and its defence minister said on Wednesday that Israeli forces will keep holding security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria indefinitely.

item.title: Nigeria's Election Campaign Turns Violent as Attacks Spread Ahead of 2027 Vote
item.description: Nigeria's campaign for elections in January has been hit by a wave of attacks on candidates, convoys and rallies, with monitors counting more than 30 incidents and at least 10 deaths since campaigning began in August.

item.title: AI Data Centres Are Turning Their Waste Heat Into Warm Homes
item.description: Engineers in Denmark have found a way to capture the vast heat thrown off by artificial intelligence computers and use it to warm homes, a hospital and factories, instead of letting it escape into the air.

item.title: Ukraine Bids Farewell to Rayana, the Mother and Drone Operator Killed on the Front Line
item.description: Ukraine has bid farewell to Rayana, a mother and former Muay Thai coach who became a drone operator with a volunteer battalion and was killed in a Russian air strike in the Donetsk region.

item.title: Critical Java Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code on Servers Without Logging In
item.description: A serious flaw in Java, the programming language that powers millions of servers, can let attackers run their own code on widely used business software without logging in, security researchers have found. Fixed builds are out, and the US cyber agency is urging organisations to patch immediately.

item.title: Philippines Files Three Child Abuse Material Charges Against Meghan's Father Thomas Markle
item.description: Police in the Philippines have filed three criminal complaints against Thomas Markle, the 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, over alleged child sexual abuse material, adding a second country's case to the federal charge he already faces in the United States.

item.title: Trump and Putin Shake Hands as All Three Leaders Appear Together in Shenzhen
item.description: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin shook hands in public for the first time in more than a year on Wednesday evening, as the three leaders appeared together in Shenzhen hours before their first-ever trilateral meeting.

item.title: World Court to Rule on Rohingya Genocide Case as Refugees Await Justice
item.description: The world's highest court will rule on Thursday whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, a decision refugees in Bangladesh have waited seven years to hear.

item.title: British Households Face £443 Annual Energy Bill Rise From January as Inflation Picks Up Again
item.description: Household energy bills in Britain are forecast to rise by £443 a year from January, taking the typical annual bill to £2,166, as the cost of living climbs again and wholesale gas prices stay high.

item.title: Ghana's $60m Presidential Jet Sparks Outrage as Critics Question Mahama's U-Turn
item.description: Ghana has taken delivery of a new presidential jet worth about $61 million, setting off a fierce public row over cost and timing as many citizens struggle with the high cost of living.

item.title: Bancroft Breaks Silence on Sandpapergate, Says Whole Australia Team Knew About Ball Tampering
item.description: Cameron Bancroft has broken his silence on the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying the whole Australian team knew sandpaper was being used against South Africa and that he became the scapegoat for the side.

item.title: Boxing Champion Jorge Linares Detained in Texas as US Immigration Opens Deportation Case
item.description: Former three-weight world boxing champion Jorge Linares is being held by US immigration authorities in Texas and faces deportation proceedings after officers detained him at El Paso International Airport on Sunday.

item.title: Arsenic Reaches Thailand's Village Wells as Mining Pollution Spreads From Myanmar
item.description: Toxic arsenic from rivers polluted by mining across the border in Myanmar has now seeped into underground water in northern Thailand, forcing the government into an emergency scramble for clean drinking water.

item.title: Forensic Expert Says Epstein Was Murdered, Not a Suicide in 2019
item.description: A forensic expert who spent years studying Jeffrey Epstein's autopsy records says the financier was strangled in his New York jail cell in 2019, a finding that challenges the official ruling that he took his own life.

item.title: Xi Pitches Free Trade at APEC Ahead of First-Ever Meeting With Trump
item.description: China's Xi Jinping used the opening of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday to champion free trade and open markets, hours before Donald Trump was due to arrive for the first three-way meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the United States.

item.title: Two Tankers Attacked in Strait of Hormuz as Two Crew Members Go Missing
item.description: Two vessels were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz this week, leaving two crew members missing and 13 injured, after a ship belonging to the shipping arm of the United Arab Emirates state oil company was struck on Tuesday evening and a gas tanker was hit twice and abandoned.

item.title: Poverty, Threats and Fear Push African Journalism to Breaking Point, Survey Finds
item.description: Most journalists across Africa cannot live on what their work pays, while threats, intimidation and self-censorship have become part of the job, according to a continent-wide survey of 1,586 journalists in 45 countries.

item.title: Category 5 Cyclone Xavier Batters Northern Cook Islands With 315 km/h Gusts
item.description: Severe Tropical Cyclone Xavier has strengthened into a Category 5 storm over the Northern Cook Islands, packing sustained winds of 220 kilometres per hour and gusts up to 315, as emergency officials urge islanders to stay on high alert.
